name: AI Shots
description: Shot-boundary detection for AI runs. Stores each analysed video file's shots in Cove, where every extension can read and edit them.
author: skier233

tutorialTopics.title: AI Shots
tutorialTopics.description: Split videos into their shots, so editors and other extensions can work shot by shot.

slides.title: Tick Shot Boundaries in Run AI
slides.caption: Select videos, open Run AI and tick Shot Boundaries. It is never ticked for you: the model reads every frame of each video, so a run takes minutes per video at 4K.
slides.bodyMarkdown: Your AI server needs a **shot boundary** model for the feature to appear. Each analysed video file gets its own shots, with each shot's type and the kind of cut that starts it.

slides.title: Existing shots are kept
slides.caption: A file that already has shots is skipped, so running again only analyses new files. To analyse a file again, tick Force rerun and replace stored data.
slides.bodyMarkdown: A forced rerun **replaces the file's shots, including any you edited by hand**. Leave Shot Boundaries unticked when you force a rerun of other features.

slides.title: Where shots are kept
slides.caption: Shots are stored in Cove, not in AI Shots, so every extension can read and edit them.
slides.bodyMarkdown: **Settings → AI Data** counts them as *Shot Boundaries* and can purge them, for example to analyse a whole library again with a newer model.
